title: Microsoft Purview Content Explorer: enhanced filter for sensitive information types and labels (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: Hold: the briefing asserts that the enhancement introduces no identity, requires no new sign-in and takes no action on content, but Microsoft does not state those guarantees. The roadmap facts, licensing requirements and role-membership controls are supported; narrow the unsupported assurances to what Microsoft actually describes.

claims.claim: This is a Microsoft Purview Information Protection Content Explorer enhancement.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview: Information Protection-Content Explorer – Enhanced Tag (SIT, Labels) Filter at UI Layer

claims.claim: The enhancement adds UI controls enabling scoped visibility and filtering of SIT and label data for discoverability and governance.
claims.quote: Introduces enhanced controls in Content Explorer’s UI, enabling scoped visibility and filtering of SIT and label data. This will help with content discoverability and governance.

claims.claim: SIT means sensitive information type and refers to pattern-based classification.
claims.quote: Sensitive information types (SITs) are pattern-based classifiers.
claims.fix: Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/sit-sensitive-information-type-learn-about for the pattern-based definition of SIT.

claims.claim: Sensitive information types recognise data such as credit card and national ID numbers.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 includes definitions for many common sensitive information types from across many different regions that are ready for you to use. For example, credit card numbers, bank account numbers, and national ID numbers.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not describe this enhancement by the roadmap's name.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview Content Explorer enhanced tag SIT labels filter 553218 518224 scoped visibility default saved views tenant switch PowerShell. Read both explorer pages and searched What's new in Microsoft Purview; no named enhancement.

claims.claim: Content Explorer (classic) already has a filter box accepting a label or sensitive information type name.
claims.quote: If you know the name of the label or the sensitive information type, type it into the filter box.

claims.claim: Content Explorer supports saved customised views configured with SITs, sensitivity labels, trainable classifiers and retention labels.
claims.quote: You can create customized views in content explorer, by configuring what SITs, Sensitivity Labels, Trainable Classifiers, and Retention Labels which are important for you.

claims.claim: A saved Content Explorer view can be made the default.
claims.quote: A view can be made default, to quickly load the view next time content explorer is opened.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not identified the documented saved views as this roadmap item.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview Content Explorer enhanced tag SIT labels filter 553218 518224 scoped visibility default saved views tenant switch PowerShell. Read Content Explorer (classic), data explorer and What's new; none connects saved views to either roadmap id.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not explained what the enhancement's scoped visibility adds to the documented saved views.
claims.quote: Searched: Content Explorer scoped visibility default identity sign-in action content; enhanced tag identity authentication actions. Read both explorer pages and What's new; found no feature-specific explanation beyond the roadmap.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; What's changing; Why it matters; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: The enhancement's default state and any change to existing role holders' visibility on arrival are not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview Content Explorer enhanced tag SIT labels filter 553218 518224 scoped visibility default saved views tenant switch PowerShell. Read both roadmap records, both explorer pages and What's new; none states the enhancement's arrival default.

claims.claim: The enhancement's rollout mechanics are not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview Content Explorer enhanced tag SIT labels filter 553218 518224 scoped visibility default saved views tenant switch PowerShell. Read the roadmap record, both explorer pages and What's new; no enhancement-specific rollout procedure.

claims.claim: Content Explorer (classic) is reached in the Microsoft Purview portal through Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Explorers > Content explorer.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Explorers > Content explorer.

claims.claim: Data explorer is reached in the Microsoft Purview portal through Solutions > Information Protection > Explorers > Data explorer.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protectionn > Explorers > Data explorer.

claims.claim: Data explorer's filter box accepts the name of a label, classifier or sensitive information type.
claims.quote: If you know the name of the label, classifiers or the sensitive information type, you can type that into the filter box.

claims.claim: Content Explorer access is highly restricted because it exposes scanned-file contents to authorised role holders.
claims.quote: Access to content explorer is highly restricted because it lets you read the contents of scanned files. Therefore, you need additional permissions to access content explorer data.

claims.claim: Content Explorer's content-viewing permissions supersede permissions locally assigned to the items.
claims.quote: These permissions supersede permissions that are locally assigned to the items, which allow viewing of the content.

claims.claim: Content Explorer List viewer membership grants visibility of items and their locations.
claims.quote: Content Explorer List viewer: Membership in this role group allows you to see each item and its location in list view.

claims.where: controls[0].governs; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Content Explorer Content viewer membership grants visibility of item contents.
claims.quote: Content Explorer Content viewer: Membership in this role group allows you to view the contents of each item in the list.

claims.claim: Content viewer permission is also required to see item names in list view.
claims.quote: Additionally, this role is also required to view name of items in list view, which might contain sensitive data.

claims.claim: The enhancement introduces no new identity.
claims.quote: Searched: Content Explorer enhanced tag identity authentication actions; Content Explorer scoped visibility default identity sign-in action content. Read both explorer pages and What's new; none states that the enhancement introduces no identity.
claims.fix: Remove 'No new identity or sign-in.' Keep the following documented Content Explorer access and administrative-unit facts.

claims.claim: The enhancement introduces no new sign-in.
claims.quote: Searched: Content Explorer enhanced tag identity authentication actions; Content Explorer scoped visibility default identity sign-in action content. Read both explorer pages and What's new; the existing portal sign-in steps do not state this enhancement's sign-in behaviour.
claims.fix: Remove 'No new identity or sign-in.' The cited pages document signing in to the existing portal, not a guarantee about the enhancement's authentication changes.

claims.where: Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Content Explorer data-classification viewer permissions can be restricted by administrative-unit assignments.
claims.quote: Content Explorer support administrative units. Members of role groups that have the data classification list viewer or data classification content viewer role receive these respective role permissions can be restricted by administrative unit assignments within content explorer.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Content Explorer filters and displays existing classified or labelled data.
claims.quote: Content explorer shows a current snapshot of the items that have a sensitivity label, a retention label, or are classified as a sensitive information type in your organization.

claims.claim: The enhancement makes no change to actions and takes no action on content.
claims.quote: Searched: Content Explorer enhanced tag identity authentication actions; Content Explorer scoped visibility default identity sign-in action content. Read both explorer pages and What's new; neither the UI-only roadmap description nor these pages guarantees no content actions.
claims.fix: Replace the Autonomy & actions bullet with 'The roadmap describes enhanced UI controls enabling scoped visibility and filtering of SIT and label data.' Remove the guarantees 'No change' and 'takes no action on content'.

claims.claim: Content Explorer counts can take up to seven days to update.
claims.quote: It can take up to seven days for counts to update in content explorer and 14 days for files that are in SharePoint.

claims.claim: Counts for SharePoint files can take up to 14 days to update.
claims.quote: It can take up to seven days for counts to update in content explorer and 14 days for files that are in SharePoint.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Data classification analytics is included in Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5, Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5 Compliance, Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5 Information Protection & Governance and Office 365 E5.
claims.quote:
| Feature | Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5, Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5 Compliance, Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5 Information Protection & Governance | Office 365 E5 |

claims.claim: E3/A3/G3 tenants receive underlying Content Explorer data aggregation rather than the E5/A5/G5 explorer interfaces.
claims.quote: While Data classification analytics (Content & Activity Explorer interfaces) requires E5/A5/G5 licensing, the underlying data aggregation continues for E3/A3/G3 tenants to support analytics and compliance scenarios.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a licence specific to this enhanced filter.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview Content Explorer enhanced filter license pricing meter E5 G5. Read Content Explorer (classic) licensing and the Purview service description's Data classification analytics section; no enhancement-specific licence.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published a meter specific to this enhanced filter.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview Content Explorer enhanced filter license pricing meter E5 G5. Read the Purview service description, Content Explorer (classic) licensing and the Purview billing models search excerpt; no enhanced-filter meter.

claims.claim: Compliance administrator, Security administrator or Compliance data administrator Entra ID membership can grant access to the Content Explorer tab.
claims.quote:
To access the content explorer tab, assign an account membership in any one of these Entra ID roles or Purview roles.
Entra ID roles
- Compliance administrator
- Security administrator
- Compliance data administrator

claims.claim: Applicable Information Protection roles and role groups can grant access to the Content Explorer tab.
claims.quote:
Here's a list of applicable role groups.
- Information Protection
- Information Protection Admins
- Information Protection Analysts
- Information Protection Investigators
- Information Protection Readers

claims.claim: Tab-access roles do not themselves grant permission to view item lists or contents.
claims.quote: Membership in these roles doesn't grant permission to view the list of items in content explorer or to view the contents of the items in content explorer.

claims.claim: The two Content Explorer role groups are independent and not cumulative, so someone needing both list and content access needs both permissions.
claims.quote: These are independent role groups and aren't cumulative. For example, if you want to grant an account the ability to view the items and their locations only, grant Content Explorer List viewer rights.

claims.claim: Role management role holders can assign Content Explorer role-group membership.
claims.quote: Role management role holders in Microsoft Purview can assign the necessary Content Explorer List Viewer, and Content Explorer Content Viewer role group membership.

claims.claim: The permissions page supports security groups for role membership only in Microsoft 365 commercial cloud organisations.
claims.quote: Security groups are supported only in Microsoft 365 commercial cloud organizations.

claims.claim: The printed Purview portal path reaches the Choose users control for adding role-group members.
claims.quote: Go to Settings > Roles and scopes ... Select Role groups. On Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions, select a Microsoft Purview role group you want to add users to. Select Edit on the control bar. On Edit members of the role group, select Choose users or Choose groups.

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity "<role-group>" -Member "<user-UPN>" adds a user to the target role group through Exchange PowerShell, including Security & Compliance.
claims.quote: Use the Add-RoleGroupMember cmdlet to add members to a management role group. The Identity parameter specifies the role group to add a member to. The Member parameter specifies who you want to add to the role group. ... User ID or user principal name (UPN)
